Formulation
Predisposing: Family history of serious illness (bowel cancer); possible baseline health anxiety.  
Precipitating: Acute gastrointestinal illness causing functional impairment and worry.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing physical symptoms, restricted activity, limited hydration/food intake, uncertainty about diagnosis.  
Protective: Good help-seeking behavior; insight; currently low risk.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Understand whether current symptoms indicate serious disease  
  • Reduce anxiety about bowel cancer  
  • Resume normal work and daily activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Decrease health-related anxiety to sub-clinical levels  
  • Support coping while physical illness resolves
- Actions (Patient):
  • Monitor symptoms and follow GP advice on hydration, diet, and rest  
  • Limit online health searches; use vetted resources (e.g., CDC, NHS)  
  • Practice simple relaxation/breathing exercises when anxious
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide clear education on likely benign cause (viral gastroenteritis)  
  • Offer brief CBT-based guidance for health anxiety (safety-seeking behaviors, thought challenging)  
  • Arrange in-person review if gastrointestinal symptoms persist >48 hrs or worsen  
  • Consider referral to psychological services if anxiety remains problematic after resolution of physical illness

Secondary Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Not recorded
- Clinical Goal(s): Not recorded
- Actions (Patient): Not recorded
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Hydration, avoidance of unnecessary antibiotics, red-flag symptoms (fever, blood in stool/vomit), reassurance re bowel cancer risk.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent or worsening diarrhoea >48 hrs, high fever, blood in stool/vomit, escalating anxiety interfering with function.
- Coping Strategies: Deep breathing, gradual return to normal diet, paced activity, contact GP if concerned.

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None at present
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable (plan generated from GP consult)
- Review Date: To be set at follow-up consult or if symptoms persist (>48 hrs)

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal mental health diagnosis, structured MSE, cognitive testing, substance use history, suicide risk question, formal goals/consent.  
● Internal conflicts: DOB/age discrepancy (1992 vs “age 48”).  
● Transcript quality notes: Consult focused on physical health; minimal mental health exploration; no demographic or contact details recorded.
